extracted.intended_audience: merchants, apprentices, and students of practical arithmetic (historical)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and conventions for performing commercial arithmetic: dividing goods, computing proportions, valuing mixed-commodity exchanges, converting units/currencies, and allocating shares and wages. The content is a historical practical-arithmetic manual with worked examples aimed at merchants and their clerks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divide quantities into parts/proportions
rubrics_metrics.description: When dividing a whole quantity into parts, convert to simple numbers/parts and divide accordingly: e.g., 'dividere fùnìliter.f.De ^oia e diraifàme de4.2.parti' and 'dividi.5 9 Cbe luna parte fia. 1 .co.laltra.3'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show dividing an amount into specified fractional parts (halves, thirds, quarters) by converting to a common count, partitioning, and then expressing each part's count and remaining remainder. Treat remainders explicitly and if necessary convert to smaller units (e.g., take a quarter, then further divide that quarter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Make values comparable by converting to a common unit
rubrics_metrics.description: To compare or combine items with different nominal sizes/values, multiply each by factors that bring them to a common basis so 'la cofa varra' can be compared: 'quello tira equalea... la cofa varra... la universal oc.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual repeatedly instructs to multiply items by numbers (e.g., by the parts or by powers like 20, 64,000) so that different parcels become 'equal' and their values sum sensibly. Use least common multiples or universal denominators; examples use multiplication and summation to obtain total comparable value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule of three / proportional equations to find unknowns
rubrics_metrics.description: Set up a proportion (equation) and solve by multiplying and dividing: 'quando... fare la equatione la cola varra... la equatione la cola varra... fare la equatione ... la radici'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a direct proportion: if A corresponds to B, then scale to find X corresponding to Y by cross-multiplication. The text mentions solving proportions by finding roots and using the equation to get the unknown, with worked numeric examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle fractional parts by converting to common denominators
rubrics_metrics.description: When working with fractions (thirds, quarters, etc.), convert to a common denominator to add, subtract, or compare: e.g., turning quarters and thirds into a common partition before adding or comparing 'un qrto cofa cauane.2 .teda un qrto co.in.2'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual demonstrates decomposing larger fractions into smaller uniform parts (e.g., express quarters as halves of halves) so that different fractional shares can be directly compared or recombined; carry through numerators and denominators stepwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocate mixed-value goods proportionally by value
rubrics_metrics.description: When goods of different kinds/qualities are to be divided, determine each part's value by converting to the same monetary unit and then allocate proportionally: 'quando... la borsa babia... la cofa valere... dirai che cauallo vale...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include assigning values to horses, bags, cloth pieces and then apportioning payments/returns based on these values; adjust for merit/quality and pro-rate shares (e.g., if one horse 'merita' more, its greater value is counted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute wages and time-pro-rated payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Pro-rate wages and payments according to time or units of service: 'li parlarij arata... il salario... la rata ... pro rata per mesi/anni', and distribute wages over months or fractions of a year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a wage is specified per period, multiply/divide to find amount for partial periods. The text gives examples of converting annual wages to monthly/daily shares and dividing those shares among claimants or time intervals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valuation of commodities by piece, roll, or weight (cloth, panno, rollo)
rubrics_metrics.description: Value cloth and textile goods by counting rolls/pieces and applying the per-roll/per-piece price, summing to a total monetary value: 'una quatita de panno... il collo ... la ualuta... una quatita de panno varra...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: count items (rolls, braccia, centinara), translate to the standard counting unit for that commodity, multiply by unit price, and adjust for color/quality (bianco/rosso) or for partial rolls. Examples include computing how many rolls equal a certain monetary sum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute fodder/consumption problems for animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine how many animals can be fed for given time with given fodder by dividing total fodder by per-animal consumption per time: 'poiciferai li caualli... quanti ne mangiaranno... quattro caualli i.6.oi mangiano.i 2.4...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual gives numerous worked cases: find per-animal per-day consumption, multiply by number of days or animals as needed, and solve by proportional scaling (if fodder increases/decreases, scale animals or time inversely).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling remainders and redistributions (exchange/compensation)
rubrics_metrics.description: When someone receives goods and later redistributes, compute net due by accounting for what was taken, returned, and remaining: 'uno fe troua vna ... li uedette... quanti ne troua e #ti oua... e quàti ne oecte al f.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track the sequence of receipts and payments step-by-step: subtract what was given away, account for those converted to money or other goods, and compute final balances (examples with eggs, money, and cloth).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjust value for quality or merit
rubrics_metrics.description: Increase or decrease valuation depending on merit/quality judgments: 'se... el cauallo el ql valtua Ducati... piu ebe no bauia meritato... lo valle...', i.e., goods of better merit get higher assigned value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text instructs to judge relative merit and assign higher counts/ducati accordingly; then use these adjusted values in the proportional sharing or sale computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use universal multipliers for scaling fractional partitions (large-power denominators)
rubrics_metrics.description: When partitions involve many subdivisions, adopt a universal multiplier (e.g., 20, 64,000) to remove fractions and operate in integers: 'la universal oc.' and examples using '64oooo' and scaling so 'la cofaicibcpofto ... 64oooo' .
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a universal denominator big enough to express all fractional parts as integers; multiply all quantities, perform integer arithmetic (add/multiply/divide), then divide back by the universal denominator to recover original-scaled results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use tabular methods when many cases recur
rubrics_metrics.description: For many repeated or similar computations, resort to a table for efficiency: 'recurre ad tabula' to handle multiple repeated cases or many variations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text suggests organizing recurring proportion computations in a table so clerks can look up results rather than recompute each time; useful for standard prices, unit conversions, or repeated proportions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convert between grains/flour and bread yield for bakers' computations
rubrics_metrics.description: When converting grain to bread or calculating how much bread will be produced from a quantity of grain, follow the specified proportions and yields: 'quando il faro val P.?f.di ... farai el pan de 4.ò...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for losses and processing yields: determine how many units of bread result from a given unit of grain, adjust for different recipes/standards, and scale prices accordingly to get cost per loaf or per weight of bread.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value small units aggregated into larger monetary units (eggs, small produce)
rubrics_metrics.description: When many small-value items (eggs, fichi) are involved, count them, determine per-item price, and aggregate into monetary units or distribute shares: numerous examples of eggs counted and turned into ducats or shares 'una uea p D.7.luno... riuedette tanti ...' .
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Method: tally small items, convert to price per unit or per group (dozen/score), multiply, and then allocate or distribute using division or proportions; treat leftover small items by converting to smaller monetary fractions if necessary.
